messages:
Ravi: Quick thread to land the penalty decay + affinity rebalance checks. We're seeing noisy swings when temporary latency spikes add penalties that outlive the spike and cause churn. Thoughts on adding a decay half-life and a separate 'rebalance_cooldown' for affinity moves?

Marta: Yes — we should separate penalty decay (how penalty value fades) from action cooldown (how often we actually move affinity). Decay can be continuous, cooldown is discrete.

Elena: Empirically, a half-life of ~45s smooths the p99 noise for our EU probes. But affinity moves need a cooldown of at least 3m to avoid thrash.

Jae: Concern: different tenants have different sensitivity. We should make both parameters tunable per-tenant-route. Defaults should be conservative.

Ravi: Proposal sketch in DSL form:
```
route "embeddings" {
  penalty_decay {
    half_life = "45s"   # how quickly measured penalty decays
    min_decay = 0.05     # floor to prevent immediate zeroing
  }
  affinity {
    rebalance_cooldown = "3m"
    max_moves_per_window = 1
    prefer_same_region = true
  }
}
```
This keeps the runtime deterministic and configurable.

Marta: Also need deterministic tie-breakers when multiple routes have similar scored penalties. Either prefer lower-cost route, or favor sticky-affinity if within epsilon. Define `tie_strategy = ["affinity","cost","latency"]`.

Elena: Good point. Add metric tags so we can audit: `route.rebalance.attempt`, `route.rebalance.success`, `route.penalty.decay.ms` with tenant/route/region. We'll be able to count thrash events.

Jae: For evaluation, add a canary roll that only applies shorter cooldowns to internal tenants. And a guardrail: do not move affinity if active request ratio > 0.2 for that tenant (to avoid migrating hot sessions).

Ravi: Suggest adding a binary guard `disallow_migration_when_hot = true` and a numeric `hot_threshold = 0.2`. Add a quick pseudo-check in runtime: if current_inflight / capacity > hot_threshold then skip rebalance.

Marta: Ops concern: Dedicated pools may want different defaults (they pay for capacity, prefer stability). Mark settings as `scope = [global, tenant, dedicated]` and surface migration notes for Dedicated customers.

Elena: On the math side, recommend using an exponential decay: new_penalty = old_penalty * 2^(-(dt/half_life)). It composes well and is cheap to compute.

Jae: We also need a graceful-backoff for rebalances that fail. If a rebalance attempt fails due to capacity, increase the cooldown multiplicatively: cooldown *= 2 up to a cap. This avoids repeated failing churn.

Ravi: Good. Add `rebalance_backoff = { factor = 2, max = "30m" }`. Also log the failure reason for replay.

Marta: Telemetry-driven autosetting idea: prod-sim should run a tuning job that sweeps half_life and rebalance_cooldown by region and tenant size, then produce recommended defaults.

routing-bot: Enqueued sim job `tune/penalty-decay-2026-03` (est runtime 4h). Results will land in #eng-sim-results.

Elena: Security note: ensure affinity moves respect tenant isolation labels and do not surface route metadata across tenants. Add a RBAC check in the policy-broker to validate a proposed move.

Jae: Implementation plan: (1) Add config surface to RouteBinding, (2) Implement exp-decay + cooldown in runtime scheduler, (3) Add metrics and backoff, (4) Sim sweep, (5) Canary on internal tenants.

Ravi: Timeline: prototype in 5 days, sim in 2 days after prototype, canary in 2 weeks. I'll author the RFC draft with examples and the deterministic tie-breaker matrix.

Marta: Sounds good. If we make defaults conservative and observable, we should reduce incident risk.

Ravi: Thanks — ending notes: keep rebalance logs idempotent and machine-parseable. I'll post RFC link when ready.
